FRAMING LOCK — EXPLICIT FRAME BOUNDARIES (this paragraph outranks the CLOSE-CROP MANDATE): photograph the front waistband and fly of the trousers with the closure UNFASTENED AND LAID OPEN, flat and front-up on a plain surface, straight on and level. TOP edge of the picture about one waistband-depth above the top of the waistband. BOTTOM edge about one waistband-depth below the bottom end of the fly. LEFT and RIGHT edges about two waistband-depths outside the two open waistband ends, so the whole opened closure — the waistband extension on one side, the under-fly on the other, and the tab bridging between them — is in frame together. GEOMETRY LOCK — the defining feature is an extra INNER TAB. It extends horizontally across from the waistband end of the under-fly, sitting just below the waistband seam and on the INSIDE of the closure, and it fastens with a single HIDDEN button that sits inside the fly and cannot be seen when the trousers are closed. The tab is about as deep as the waistband is deep and roughly twice as long as it is deep, with a squared end and a worked buttonhole in it. A second buttonhole sits in the waistband extension above. Negative: NOT a plain single-button waistband, NOT a hook-and-bar closure, NOT an extended pointed or curved waistband tab worn on the OUTSIDE — this tab is an interior one; no exposed metal zip pull dominating the frame.
